knowledge_point.title: Calculating the Slope of a Tangent Line of a Curve at a Given Point

question.:question/problem:
Find $m,$ the slope of the tangent to the curve $y=k(x)$ at the point where $x=0.$

We have $k(x)=-x^{3} -3 x + 5 e^{x}$ and $k^{\prime}(x)=-3 x^{2} + 5 e^{x} -3.$

$m=$
{{field-1}}
question.:question/worked-solution:
We have $k(x)=-x^{3} -3 x + 5 e^{x}.$ The slope of the tangent at $x=0$ is equal to $k^{\prime}(0).$ The given derivative is

$$
k^{\prime}(x)=-3 x^{2} + 5 e^{x} -3.
$$

Now, we evaluate at $x=0$ and get

$$
\begin{aligned}k^{\prime}(0) & =-3 (0)^{2} + 5 e^{(0)} -3 \\ & =-3+0+5 \\ & =2.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the slope of the tangent to the curve is $2.$

question.:question/worked-solution:
Let $f(x)=-3 x^{2} + \frac{1}{\left(x -1\right)^{2}}.$ The slope of the tangent at $x=4$ is equal to $f^{\prime}(4).$ Computing the derivative, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}f^{\prime}(x) & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(-3 x^{2} + \frac{1}{\left(x -1\right)^{2}}) \\ & =-6x+(-2(x-1)^{-3}) \\ & =-6 x -\frac{2}{\left(x -1\right)^{3}}.\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we evaluate at $x=4$ and get

$$
\begin{aligned}f^{\prime}(4) & =-6 (4) -\frac{2}{\left((4) -1\right)^{3}} \\ & =-24-\frac{2}{27} \\ & =-\frac{650}{27}.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the slope $m$ of the tangent to the curve at $x=4$ is

$$
m=f^{\prime}(4)=-\frac{650}{27}.
$$

question.:question/worked-solution:
Let $f(x)=-4 x^{2} + \frac{1}{\left(x -3\right)^{2}}.$ The slope of the tangent at $x=2$ is equal to $f^{\prime}(2).$ Computing the derivative, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}f^{\prime}(x) & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(-4 x^{2} + \frac{1}{\left(x -3\right)^{2}}) \\ & =-8x+(-2(x-3)^{-3}) \\ & =-8 x -\frac{2}{\left(x -3\right)^{3}}.\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we evaluate at $x=2$ and get

$$
\begin{aligned}f^{\prime}(2) & =-8 (2) -\frac{2}{\left((2) -3\right)^{3}} \\ & =-16+2 \\ & =-14.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the slope $m$ of the tangent to the curve at $x=2$ is

$$
m=f^{\prime}(2)=-14.
$$

question.:question/problem: Find the slope of the tangent to the curve $y=2 x^{7} -5 x^{5} -8188 x$ at the point where $x=3.$
question.:question/worked-solution:
Let $f(x)=2 x^{7} -5 x^{5} -8188 x.$ The slope of the tangent at $x=3$ is equal to $f^{\prime}(3).$ Computing the derivative, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}f^{\prime}(x) & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(2 x^{7} -5 x^{5} -8188 x) \\ & =14 x^{6} -25 x^{4} -8188.\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we evaluate at $x=3$ and get

$$
\begin{aligned}f^{\prime}(3) & =14 (3)^{6} -25 (3)^{4} -8188 \\ & =-8188-2025+10206 \\ & =-7.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the slope of the tangent to the curve is $-7.$

question.:question/worked-solution:
Let $f(x)=2 x^{6} -3 x^{4} + 6 x^{2} -4.$ The slope of the tangent at $x=2$ is equal to $f^{\prime}(2).$ Computing the derivative, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}f^{\prime}(x) & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(2 x^{6} -3 x^{4} + 6 x^{2} -4) \\ & =12x^{5}-3(4x^{3})+6(2x)-0 \\ & =12 x^{5} -12 x^{3} + 12 x.\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we evaluate at $x=2$ and get

$$
\begin{aligned}f^{\prime}(2) & =12 (2)^{5} -12 (2)^{3} + 12 (2) \\ & =-96+24+384 \\ & =312.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the slope $m$ of the tangent to the curve at $x=2$ is

$$
m=f^{\prime}(2)=312.
$$
